Artefact 001 · v1.0 · Preliminary

Business Problem & Project Context

Frame the problem without assuming that buying or configuring a particular CRM is automatically the right answer.

Independent simulation. Northstar is a fictional service organisation. These are scenario-based observations and hypotheses, not results from an actual client investigation.

Scenario facts

Northstar receives prospective-customer enquiries through website, WhatsApp, telephone, referrals and marketing campaigns. Website enquiries reach a shared Sales inbox; two salespeople handle WhatsApp; referrals can go directly to individuals; Marketing exports campaign leads to spreadsheets. Sales representatives maintain records in spreadsheets, email and notes. Support has a separate ticketing tool, and management receives a weekly Excel report.

Management reports inconsistent follow-ups, fragmented customer information and difficulty producing reliable conversion reports. Duplicate records may exist, but their incidence is unknown.

Initial business problem

Customer and prospect information is handled through different channels and storage methods. Without first understanding lead ownership, information standards, handoffs and the reporting process, Northstar cannot determine whether process, information management, or systems are primarily responsible for its reported concerns.

Business need

An agreed way to record, maintain, appropriately share and analyse lead/customer information across relevant teams, with clear responsibilities and controls.

Objectives to validate

  1. Make enquiries identifiable and traceable from receipt to disposition.
  2. Agree ownership and follow-up expectations.
  3. Provide authorised roles with appropriate customer history.
  4. Define consistent sales and conversion metrics.
  5. Investigate and manage data completeness, duplicates and consistency.

Scope and boundaries

Investigate now

Lead intake, assignment, follow-up, Sales/Support interfaces, storage practices, reporting definitions, data ownership and possible data-quality gaps.

Not claimed or implemented

No vendor chosen; no real interviews, production CRM setup, API integration, measured ROI or verified customer-data improvement.

Initial hypotheses

  • Different channel practices may produce inconsistent customer records.
  • Ownership and follow-up rules may be unclear or inconsistently followed.
  • Sales and Support may lack appropriately shared customer history.
  • Weekly reporting may suffer from data-definition or consolidation problems.

Open questions

What are enquiry volumes and lead definitions? Who assigns and reassigns ownership? How are duplicates identified? What feeds the weekly Excel report? Which information may be shared across teams, under what permissions and privacy rules?

Artefact 002 · v1.0 · Planned, not executed

Stakeholder & Investigation Plan

Identify whose perspective and evidence we need before writing requirements or confirming causes.

Status: This is a proposed stakeholder map and discovery plan. No interviews, workshops, observation sessions or data reviews have yet been conducted with real Northstar employees.

Provisional stakeholder groups

GroupInformation to obtainProposed technique
Executive sponsorBusiness outcomes, constraints, investment priorities, success criteriaInterview
Sales managerLead lifecycle, ownership, follow-up targets, KPI/report issuesInterview + report review
Sales representativesActual enquiry handling, notes, workarounds, status updatesInterviews + observation + workshop
MarketingCampaign intake, lead-source attribution, handoffs and exportsInterview + document/data review
Customer SupportTicket history, customer identifiers, case handoffs, access needsInterview + ticket review
IT / Systems / DataSystem inventory, storage, access, integration, securityInterview + technical documentation

Discovery questions

  1. Walk through an enquiry from arrival to first action. Who handles it?
  2. Where and how is it recorded by channel?
  3. Who assigns ownership, and how is reassignment controlled?
  4. Which fields are required and which are frequently missing?
  5. How are enquiry, lead, opportunity, customer and case defined?
  6. How are duplicate or repeat enquiries handled?
  7. What follow-up expectations exist, and how is performance evidenced?
  8. What is transferred between Sales and Support, and when?
  9. How is the weekly Excel report prepared, checked and interpreted?
  10. What access, retention, privacy and implementation constraints apply?

Triangulation and validation

Compare stakeholder descriptions against available spreadsheets, ticket histories, timestamp records, existing procedures and observation where access is permitted. Record disagreements as questions rather than silently treating one person's account as fact. The provisional As-Is model should be reviewed in a facilitated cross-functional session.

Risks to avoid

  • Leading stakeholders by asking whether Salesforce is the answer.
  • Confusing the manager's intended workflow with employees' actual workflow.
  • Assuming separate systems necessarily mean broken integration.
  • Assigning high/low influence ratings before decision rights are understood.

Artefact 004 · v1.0 · Completed case-study specification

Requirements Catalogue & Traceability

A scoped, solution-neutral requirements specification for Sales enquiry visibility and ownership—connecting stakeholder needs to rules, system behaviour, data and proposed acceptance criteria.

Evidence boundary: Northstar is fictional. The author-selected rules form a coherent case-study baseline, not a stakeholder-approved business specification. No interviews, CRM deployment or execution of acceptance tests are claimed. The hypothetical change analysis and validation-question dispositions are completed documentation, not unresolved publication tasks.
Session 4 artefact finalisedSimulated requirementsNo production implementation

Business objective & scoped need

BO-02 · Business objective

Strengthen lead ownership and follow-up visibility

Support clear accountability and visibility of Sales enquiry ownership.

GAP-02 · Candidate gap

Enquiry capture, ownership and follow-up

Consider how unassigned enquiries can be identified and how ownership is recorded.

The defined case-study need is to identify unassigned Sales enquiries and provide appropriate visibility of enquiry ownership. These are simulated objectives and requirements, not stakeholder-approved findings.

Candidate functional requirements

IDRequired behaviourSupports
FR-001Show New AND unassigned Sales enquiries to an authorised Sales Manager.SR-001 / BR-001
FR-002Show a signed-in Sales Representative their assigned enquiries, including Closed records under the selected exercise assumption.SR-002 / BR-002
FR-003Exclude Closed enquiries from the separate Active Enquiry List.SR-003 / BR-003
FR-004Display each active-list enquiry's owner, or the label Unassigned if the owner reference is unset.SR-003 / AS-02
FR-005Prevent a new unassigned Sales enquiry changing status to Contacted.SR-004 / BR-004

Four simulated stakeholder requirements, four business rules, five functional requirements and three supporting data requirements are linked in the full catalogue. No automatic assignment, date filter or unsupported performance dashboard was introduced.

Two distinct views, two distinct rules

My Assigned Enquiries

Includes records owned by the signed-in representative regardless of status. In AC-002, Sales Rep A sees ENQ-501 and ENQ-504 (Closed), but not ENQ-502 or ENQ-503.

Selected case-study rule: AS-03 / BR-002

Active Enquiry List

Excludes records with status Closed. This does not mean that only Open records qualify. In AC-003, ENQ-501, ENQ-503 and ENQ-505 appear; ENQ-504 does not.

Selected case-study rule: AS-04 / BR-003

Acceptance criteria: testing both conditions

AC-001 checks the candidate New Unassigned Enquiries view using five synthetic records. Both conditions must match simultaneously.

RecordStatusOwnerExpected result
ENQ-601NewUnassignedInclude
ENQ-602NewSales Rep AExclude
ENQ-603In ProgressUnassignedExclude
ENQ-604NewUnassignedInclude
ENQ-605NewSales Rep BExclude

Given the authorised Sales Manager is signed in and these records exist, when the Manager opens New Unassigned Enquiries, then only ENQ-601 and ENQ-604 are shown. The expected results are proposed criteria, not evidence of an executed test.

The full Markdown catalogue also links supporting data requirements DR-001–DR-003.

Completed simulated change analysis — CR-001

The original My Assigned Enquiries exercise includes Closed records. A hypothetical stakeholder later requested excluding them from that view. The analysis identified that ENQ-504 would change from included to excluded; FR-002, BR-002, AC-002 and related tests would need review.

The potential change was assessed for business rationale, view behaviour, history access, outstanding follow-ups, scope, delivery impact and traceability. It was not adopted into the v1.0 case-study baseline, and no real approval/rejection is claimed. CR-001 is complete as a documented training analysis, not an active change awaiting a decision.

Validation-question register: documented dispositions

Session 4 identified twelve questions a real BA would investigate. All twelve have explicit dispositions for this limited fictional case study; none is presented as completed real stakeholder validation.

QuestionsCase-study disposition
Lifecycle statuses, assignment rights and permissions (OQ-01, 02, 05)Bounded by stated assumptions; full policy and workflow modelling excluded.
In Progress unassigned exceptions; Closed enquiries with follow-ups (OQ-03, 04)Analysed as training cases; no additional feature adopted.
Mandatory data fields, duplicates and follow-up definitions (OQ-06–08)Minimum necessary fields included; deeper data and activity modelling assigned to later phases.
KPIs, Sales–Support handoffs, NFRs and solution choice (OQ-09–12)Explicitly outside this view-level specification; no unevidenced solution/threshold invented.

Non-functional considerations & limitations

Security, performance, auditability, accessibility, privacy and retention were considered as quality categories, but no unsupported latency targets, full permission matrix or legal compliance assertions were manufactured. Later phases may establish measurable criteria with appropriate evidence.

Completion statement: The bounded Session 4 requirements specification, impact analysis and validation-question dispositions are complete for a fictional portfolio case study. Later customer-data, CRM and testing activities are separate workstreams—not missing Session 4 tasks.

Artefact 005 · Finalised case-study analysis · Customer Data & SQL

Customer Data Model & Data Quality Analysis

From enquiry records to a simple customer–enquiry model: documenting data, investigating broken references with SQL, reconciling submission lists and proposing sensible validation rules.

Session 5 analysis completedSynthetic SQLite evidenceNo production implementation
Evidence boundary: Northstar Services is fictional. All records, names, identifiers, findings and controls are invented for this independent case study. The SQL was checked against synthetic local fixtures only; this is not live client data, a deployed database, real stakeholder approval or CRM implementation.

Why this analysis matters

Northstar's earlier scenario raised concerns about fragmented customer information and inconsistent enquiry handling. This artefact responds to BO-01 (consistent enquiry/customer-data capture) and GAP-01 (customer-information consistency), while respecting the enquiry ownership baseline defined in Artefact 004.

Problem to investigate

Missing or inconsistent information

A customer may lack a relevant contact field, or an enquiry may refer to a customer that cannot be found.

Approach

Define → query → compare → investigate

Describe the data, run checks, document synthetic exceptions and propose controls without guessing the root cause.

Proposed logical data model

Entity 1

Customers

customer_id — unique customer identifier

name — customer name

phone — contact telephone number

Entity 2

Enquiries

enquiry_id — unique enquiry identifier

customer_id — link to customer

status — enquiry stage

assigned_owner_id — Sales owner, nullable

1 customer → many enquiries · linked by customer_id

Critical distinction: an enquiry can reference a valid customer and still be unassigned to a Sales Representative. Artefact 004 explicitly allows a missing assigned_owner_id in some cases; this document does not relabel those cases as data-quality failures.

SQL: identify the differences

Q-01 · Missing phone values

SELECT Customers.customer_id, Customers.name
FROM Customers
WHERE phone IS NULL;

Expected: C-102 | Rahul

Q-02 · Enquiries without a matching customer

SELECT Enquiries.enquiry_id
FROM Enquiries
LEFT JOIN Customers
  ON Enquiries.customer_id = Customers.customer_id
WHERE Customers.customer_id IS NULL;

Expected: ENQ-203, ENQ-204

Q-03 · Recorded Customer ID, but no customer match

SELECT Enquiries.enquiry_id
FROM Enquiries
LEFT JOIN Customers
  ON Enquiries.customer_id = Customers.customer_id
WHERE Customers.customer_id IS NULL
  AND Enquiries.customer_id IS NOT NULL;

Expected: ENQ-203 only

The second condition excludes ENQ-204, because that enquiry has no Customer ID stored at all. The full document includes separate missing-reference, matching-record and duplicate-signal queries.

Reconciliation: website vs Sales

A separate synthetic dataset compares website submission IDs with IDs recorded in Sales for the same assumed period. This is not represented as a verified operational feed or integration.

Source A

WEB-301 · WEB-302 · WEB-303 · WEB-304 · WEB-305

WEB-301 · WEB-302 · WEB-304

3 destination IDs

Reconciliation result: WEB-303 and WEB-305 are absent from the sample Sales register. That is a data discrepancy, not proof that software transfer failed. The next BA action is to check period/filter definitions, source evidence, rejection rules and any available processing logs.

SELECT WebsiteSubmissions.submission_id
FROM WebsiteSubmissions
LEFT JOIN SalesEnquiryRegister
  ON WebsiteSubmissions.submission_id = SalesEnquiryRegister.submission_id
WHERE SalesEnquiryRegister.submission_id IS NULL

Expected: WEB-303, WEB-305

Data-quality findings

IDSynthetic exceptionInterpretationRecommended BA action
DQ-01C-102 phone is NULLPotential completeness issue, depending on channel rulesConfirm required contact details and inspect source
DQ-02ENQ-203 refers to C-999Recorded but unmatched customer referenceTrace entry, import and matching rules
DQ-03ENQ-204 has NULL customer_idMissing stored customer referenceReview new-customer and incomplete-entry workflows
DQ-04WEB-303 and WEB-305 absent in SalesCross-source differenceInvestigate period, filtering and rejects

Accuracy, timeliness, privacy compliance and confirmed customer duplication cannot be assessed from these records. A phone-number match is at most a duplicate-review signal, not grounds for automatic merging.

Candidate validation and review controls

IDProposed approachQuestion before approval
VAL-01New enquiries reference an existing Customer IDHow do first-time customers get registered before their enquiry is accepted?
VAL-02Check required contact fields for the chosen channelIs phone required, or can another contact method be valid?
VAL-03Ensure unique Enquiry IDsHow are source-system IDs generated or reconciled?
REC-01Compare submission IDs for an agreed periodWho owns exception reviews and how are delays handled?
REV-01Review possible duplicates before mergingWhich matching criteria and approvals are appropriate?
Important workflow exception: A strict rule requiring an already-existing customer can inadvertently block a new customer's first enquiry. A customer-creation or provisional-capture process must be designed before VAL-01 can be approved. These rules are proposals, not additions to an approved production baseline.

Completion boundaries and next work

Session 5 has produced a reviewable logical model, data dictionary, synthetic SQL investigation, two-source reconciliation, data-quality findings and candidate controls. The underlying fixtures were checked locally with SQLite. No Salesforce implementation, live integration, stakeholder sign-off, UAT or measurable business benefit is claimed.

Artefact 006 · Proposed case-study design · CRM MVP V1

Proposed CRM Data & Solution Design

Translating Northstar's scoped enquiry-management requirements into a practical, limited CRM demonstration plan — without claiming that any Salesforce configuration has been performed.

Session 6 design prepared Design decisions still open No CRM build or UAT
Evidence boundary: Northstar Services is fictional. Artefact 006 is an independent proposed solution design based on simulated requirements and synthetic examples. No real customer, stakeholder approval, Salesforce deployment, configured validation rule, executed UAT or measured outcome is claimed.

Purpose and MVP boundary

Earlier requirements work defined a deliberately bounded scope for enquiry ownership and visibility; the data analysis examined synthetic customer–enquiry records. This design connects those findings to candidate CRM objects, fields, relationships, views, validations and future test scenarios.

Proposed MVP V1

What we plan to demonstrate

Capture synthetic Sales enquiries, maintain business-assigned owners, support scoped manager/representative views and enforce the New → Contacted ownership prerequisite.

Not part of this evidence

What has not been built

No Salesforce object configuration, integrations, API calls, reminders, dashboards, executed tests, live customer records or production environment.

Logical entities and relationships

Logical entity 1

Customer

customer_id — stable unique reference

name — customer label

phone — contact number; mandatory rule unresolved

Logical entity 2

Sales Enquiry

enquiry_id — unique reference

customer_id — proposed optional customer association

status — enquiry lifecycle value

assigned_owner_id — potentially unset business assignment

One Customer → Zero or many linked Enquiries

Each enquiry can reference at most one customer in this logical model. An optional Lookup is a candidate Salesforce relationship if Northstar explicitly adopts an identity-pending enquiry workflow. This remains an open decision (D-01), not a silently approved change to Artefact 005's candidate VAL-01.

Two different relationships: customer_id identifies the associated customer; assigned_owner_id identifies the responsible Sales representative. Missing ownership does not automatically break a valid customer link. Salesforce platform record ownership also must not be assumed equivalent to the nullable business assignment field.

Object mappings are alternatives under investigation. This document does not claim a custom Enquiry object was selected or created.

Business rules mapped to proposed CRM behaviour

RequirementProposed behaviour
BR-001 / FR-001New Unassigned view shows enquiries with status = New AND business owner unset.
BR-002 / FR-002My Assigned Enquiries includes all records assigned to the signed-in representative, including Closed.
BR-003 / FR-003Active Enquiry List excludes Closed records; Open is not the only eligible non-Closed status.
FR-004Show owner identity or the display label Unassigned.
BR-004 / FR-005Reject a requested New → Contacted transition when business owner is unset.

BR-004 — business-rule pseudocode

IF current_status = "New"
   AND requested_status = "Contacted"
   AND assigned_owner_id is unset
THEN reject the requested transition;
     prompt: "Assign a Sales representative before changing
              this enquiry to Contacted."
ELSE BR-004 alone does not block the action.

Validation is not automation. Assigning a Sales representative does not automatically change an enquiry's status. A separate authorised action must request that status change. This logic is not a deployed or tested Salesforce formula.
